newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy 1997 growth to struggle to pass 1pct - Fossa.
newsitem.headline: Italy 1997 growth to struggle to pass 1pct - Fossa.

text.p: The head of Italy's employers' organisation Confindustria said on Thursday gross domestic product growth would struggle to clear one percent this year.
"In 1997 it will be difficult to go beyond one percent," Giorgio Fossa told a news conference. "In 1998, we estimate it at 1.8 percent and in 1999 at 2.3 percent."
"They are weak results that will find it hard to boost employment," he said.
The government has targeted 1997 GDP growth of 1.2 percent, followed by 2.0 percent in 1998 and 2.5 percent in 1999.
Industry Minister Pierluigi Bersani said on Wednesday that the latest industrial orders and turnover data was good but Italy still had its work cut out to reach the GDP target.
Italian industrial orders rose 14.5 percent year-on-year in April while turnover rose 9.1 percent, national statistics institute Istat said on Wednesday.
Bersani and Prime Minister Romano Prodi both said the data confirmed the beginnings of an economic upturn.
Bersani said, however, that the 1997 GDP goal remained a very demanding objective. Treasury Minister Carlo Azeglio Ciampi has said it is credible and achievable.
